```{r}
#| label: setup-site
#| include: false
#| cache: false

# Install/load packages if needed
if (!requireNamespace("showtext", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("showtext")
}
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggplot2")
}

if (!requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("systemfonts")
}

library(showtext)
library(ggplot2)
library(systemfonts)

## Clean the slate
systemfonts::clear_local_fonts()
systemfonts::clear_registry()


# Add three Google Fonts
# Arguments: font family name, Google Font name
font_add_google("Modak", "Modak")
font_add_google("Fredoka", "Fredoka")
font_add_google("Quicksand", "Quicksand")

# Tell R to use showtext for all subsequent plots
showtext_auto()

# Optional: set DPI for raster devices (adjust if you need high-res PNGs)
showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

# Set a site-wide ggplot theme using the loaded fonts
ggplot2::theme_set(
  ggplot2::theme_bw(
    base_size = 14,
    base_family = "Modak"
  )
)

## Set the ggplot theme
theme_madhatter <- function(){ 

    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    
    theme_sub_axis(title = element_text(family = "Modak", size = 8, colour = "#2b2b2b"),
                   text = element_text(family = "Modak", size = 6, colour = "#2b2b2b")) + 
    
    theme_sub_legend(text = element_text(family = "Modak", size = 6),
                     title = element_text(family = "Quicksand", size = 8),
                     background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF0F5", colour = NA)) + 
    
    theme_sub_plot(title = element_text(family = "Modak", size = 14, colour = "#E60033"),
                   title.position = "plot",
                   subtitle = element_text(family = "Fredoka", size = 10, colour = "#d6336c"),
                   caption = element_text(family = "Quicksand", size = 6),
                   caption.position = "plot",
                   background = element_rect(fill = "#FFF0F5", colour = NA)) +
    
    theme_sub_panel(background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
                    border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "#2b2b2b", linewidth = 0.8),
                    grid.major = element_line(colour = "#FFD1DC", linewidth = 0.3),
                    grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    
    theme_sub_strip(background = element_rect(fill = "#FFB6C8", colour = "#2b2b2b"),
                    text = element_text(family = "Fredoka", size = 8))
}

## Set the theme for all plots
ggplot2::theme_set(theme_madhatter())
## Hello Kitty-ish colours for bars, boxes, points etc.
kitty <- c("#E60033", "#FFB6C8", "#FFD700", "#2b2b2b", "#87CEEB", "#d6336c")
options(ggplot2.discrete.fill = kitty,
        ggplot2.discrete.colour = kitty)

## Update the fonts for geoms as well!
## Use available fonts in ggplot label and text within the ggplot geoms 
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults(geom = "text", new = list(
  family = "Modak",
  face = "plain",
  size = 8/ggplot2::.pt, # Converting 8 points to "mm" default
  color = "#2b2b2b"
)
)
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults(geom = "label", new = list(
  family = "Modak",
  face = "plain",
  size = 8/ggplot2::.pt, # Converting 8 points to "mm" default
  color = "#2b2b2b"
)
)


```
